root_causes.description: The frontend container was forcibly terminated ('Killing: Stopping container frontend') and immediately replaced by a freshly scheduled pod frontend-76cbddfbcc-zm8l8, causing the frontend server request rate to collapse mid-window (p50 ~8 req/s vs. a window mean of ~148 req/s). Error rate and CPU stayed normal, indicating a container-level crash/restart rather than a resource or downstream fault.

evidence.observed_value: Killing: Stopping container frontend (count=1), followed by SuccessfulCreate: Created pod: frontend-76cbddfbcc-zm8l8, Pulled, Created, Started: Container started (count=1)
evidence.expected_baseline: no container kill / pod replacement events during steady state

evidence.observed_value: p50=8.009 req/s vs mean=148.190 req/s (p95=432.873, max=604.823); request rate collapses mid-window

evidence.expected_baseline: no CPU saturation; rules out cpu_stress
consistent with container replacement via pod recreation rather than in-place restart

remediation_steps: Confirm the frontend pod restart/crash: kubectl -n otel-demo get pods -l app=frontend and kubectl describe pod frontend-76cbddfbcc-zm8l8 (inspect Last State, Reason, Exit Code).
Inspect the terminated frontend container's previous logs (kubectl logs <prior-frontend-pod> --previous) to distinguish OOMKill, liveness-probe kill, or application crash.
Verify frontend readiness/liveness probe thresholds and resource limits to prevent premature container termination.
Confirm recovery: monitor frontend request rate returning to ~148 req/s and absence of further 'Killing: Stopping container frontend' events.
